gaps.sentence: He kept ___ even though everyone had left.
He ran so fast that we lost ___ of him.
gaps.explanation: 'lose sight of somebody' = no longer see them.

gaps.sentence: You ___ have seen a doctor sooner.
gaps.explanation: 'should have + participle' criticises a past decision.

gaps.sentence: It was ___ a good film that we saw it twice.
Not only ___ the tickets overpriced, but the seating was appalling.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only' at the front inverts the verb: Not only were the tickets… but…

gaps.sentence: Hardly ___ he finished speaking when the audience erupted.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly' at the front inverts the past perfect: Hardly had he finished… when…

gaps.sentence: The letters ___ delivered every morning at eight.
